answer: The nectar test I would run is proof of unique coastguard auxiliary patrol hours with service attestation: patrol hours the service logged across a full season, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so patrol hours the service logged across a full season stays private; the horizon is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the bridge of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
